summary: Scoping call to align on concrete POC plan for capacity sizing and autoscaling. Customer runs chat-like telemetry agents: steady concurrency ~40 qps, short median prompts ~220 tokens and occasional long-context up to 1k tokens, transient spikes up to ~250 qps. Redwood proposed reserved baseline plus a pre-reserved burst pool to avoid multi-minute cold starts; discussed tiered fallbacks (30s queue, quantized model fallback, last-resort cross-region). Agreed benchmarks (warm/cold KV cache, quantized vs FP16) and a target timeline: sizing doc within 48h, data by 5 days, SE test week around 2027-09-20, 2-week benchmark window, then 6-week pilot if accepted.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Type: POC scoping (capacity/autoscale)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Oscar Patel (Redwood); Priya Desai, Ethan Morales, Sofia Alvarez (Northstar)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Thanks for making time. Quick intros?
[00:05] Priya Desai: Priya, head of platform. Ethan and Sofia with me.
[00:09] Ethan Morales: Ethan, ML eng.
[00:11] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, infra lead. Can hear an echo but ok.
[00:14] Liam O'Neill: Liam here, SE, I'll run through autoscale and the benchmark harness.
[00:18] Maya Chen: We want to define success criteria up front. Priya, what's top priority?
[00:24] Priya Desai: Latency and predictable cost. We want p95 around 60ms and p99 under 150ms for our short prompts. Cost target for baseline throughput plus normal bursts should stay under about $250-300 per 1M tokens. Also must show audit logs and SSO/KMS for security review.
[00:40] Oscar Patel: Noted. We'll include SOC2 docs and KMS notes.
[00:43] Ethan Morales: Important: quality must be preserved. If quantization yields >2% regression on our eval set that's a no-go.
[00:51] Maya Chen: Understood. Typical approach for POC: size a reserved baseline sized for steady concurrency and add a pre-reserved burst pool. That avoids long cold-starts. For an initial proposal we sketched 2 reserved GPUs with a burst pool up to 6 for short tests, but we'll convert that to three cost/config options.
[01:10] Sofia Alvarez: How does the burst pool get provisioned if we're in a private VPC? We don't want resources spun up outside our peered network.
[01:20] Liam O'Neill: Two ways: pre-reserve burst capacity inside your VPC (we can provision extra nodes in your subnet during POC) or use hosted fallback in same region. For production you'd likely want pre-reserved burst in your VPC to meet residency/latency needs. For POC we can use anonymized cross-region hosted fallback if you approve.
[01:38] Priya Desai: Cross-region for POC might be ok with anonymized traces, but production must be in-region. We'll confirm.
[01:44] Maya Chen: We'll flag cross-region as contingent on security approval.
[01:47] Ethan Morales: Traffic profile: median 220 tokens, tail to 1k tokens. Steady ~40 qps; burst up to ~250 qps during customer syncs lasting 2-5 minutes. That burst shape affects autoscale config.
[02:03] Liam O'Neill: That profile is helpful. Autoscaler tuning: if bursts are short, we prefer a short queue window and aggressive scaling from pre-warm pool. If bursts are sustained, we'll route more to burst pool or scale more reserved nodes. KV cache warming is key: warm cache tests will show much lower p99s.
[02:20] Maya Chen: For fallbacks we recommend a tiered plan: 1) short queue (30s) with exponential backoff; 2) shift lower-priority traffic to quantized model variant in the pre-reserved burst pool; 3) as last resort, cross-region hosted nodes. Each fallback emits telemetry tagged as degraded-quality events.
[02:42] Sofia Alvarez: We want the ability to throttle premium vs non-premium customers during spikes. Can Redwood route by customer id?
[02:49] Oscar Patel: Yes, routing policies can be per-token or per-customer. We can route low-priority customers to queued buckets or to cheaper model variants. We'll include sample routing rules in the docs.
[03:01] Priya Desai: On cost, can you break out expected cost per 1M tokens for each config?
[03:06] Maya Chen: Yes. We'll send a spreadsheet with conservative, balanced, and aggressive configs showing reserved/burst counts, expected throughput, p99 estimates and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:16] Ethan Morales: Benchmark asks: please capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens, and quality deltas on our eval set. Run warm and cold cache variants and quantized vs FP16.
[03:28] Liam O'Neill: We'll run those. Also show cold-start tail when spinning from zero. If you pre-reserve burst nodes the cold-start is basically eliminated.
[03:38] Maya Chen: Timeline I'm proposing: sizing spreadsheet in 48 hours, Northstar uploads traces in 5 days, SE-led test runs week of 2027-09-20, two-week benchmark window, and then a six-week pilot if acceptance criteria met.
[03:52] Priya Desai: Acceptance criteria: p99 < 150ms on short profile across >= 80% of steady windows; quality regressions <= 2%; cost <= $300 / 1M tokens for expected workload.
[04:06] Sofia Alvarez: For the POC we'll accept limited cross-region testing with anonymized data only. Production cannot use cross-region.
[04:13] Oscar Patel: Noted and we'll mark that in the plan.
[04:17] Ethan Morales: Also include long-context tests of 1k tokens to watch memory pressure and queueing behavior.
[04:23] Liam O'Neill: We'll run short and long profiles and share CSV/Grafana exports with the report.
[04:29] Maya Chen: Any other open questions?
[04:33] Priya Desai: Nothing else. Looking forward to the spreadsheet.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with links and next steps. Thanks everyone.
[04:40] (Call ends)

Notes: Auto-transcription mis-typed some terms ("KV cache" sometimes tokenized as "K V cache"). Brief crosstalk at 00:11. Shared artifacts: sizing spreadsheet (link placeholder), benchmark harness repo (link placeholder), SOC2 summary (link placeholder).
